setup_data_boundary.title: Prepare upstream or keep an existing game build
setup_data_boundary.instruction: Use your own Advance Wars USA Rev 1 original with the upstream Windows alpha guide. Run Setup.cmd deliberately; it records setup.log, skips completed work and can be resumed. The generated Advance Wars (recomp).cmd launches the prepared game. For native registration, choose build/Release/AWRE.exe, use the prepared project root as working directory and game/aw.gba as the argument in Change launch details. Compiler tools are not the game; the reviewed alpha has no audio.

setup_data_boundary.title: Keep your files and update through upstream
setup_data_boundary.instruction: Use a separate folder you control and retain your working copy. An existing native player can use Portcove’s non-owning registration after the read-only executable review; choose Play separately. You or upstream keep runtime updates, original files, generated data, saves and settings. Portcove does not replace, back up or roll back this external runtime. Follow the selected upstream version’s instructions when changing it.

Register only a native game output you have prepared with its required working folder, not a Python disc or compiler tool.

setup_data_boundary.title: Use the appropriate runtime
setup_data_boundary.instruction: This reconstructs the DOS Theme Hospital executable. Its hospital.exe/hosp.exe outputs use DOS/4GW and DOSBox; they are not native Windows players to register directly. Before following the source build, establish the needed input and toolchain/component permissions: the guide names its accepted GOG offline installer/HOSPITAL.EXE, its first Nix shell downloads proprietary Watcom 10.5/10.6 CDs, and tools GPL does not grant rights to reconstructed, Miles, Smacker or Watcom code. An owned GOG copy alone does not settle every component. The conditional DOS build/run guide remains upstream; Portcove invokes no installer or toolchain. For a distinct managed native alternative, find CorsixTH in Discover.

The supported extracted default.xbe SHA-256 is 3cfd001a84fc3e08175d6c4b2e42ebf49577a089b5d0bd87ac724f61a41816bc; the reviewed guide does not support other dumps. Its XDVDFS/code-generation steps and local build are deliberate upstream actions. Use the documented native play invocation with --disc and its interactive/Vulkan options, preserving the prepared working folder and data. Register only that prepared native runtime. Other platforms and full-game behavior need separate evidence.

setup_data_boundary.title: Keep your files and update through upstream
setup_data_boundary.instruction: Use a separate folder you control and retain your working copy. An existing native player can use Portcove’s non-owning registration after the read-only executable review; choose Play separately. You or upstream keep runtime updates, original files, generated data, saves and settings. Portcove does not replace, back up or roll back this external runtime. Follow the selected upstream version’s instructions when changing it.

setup_data_boundary.title: Prepare upstream or keep an existing game build
setup_data_boundary.instruction: Follow upstream's recursive gcnrecomp/build guide with your own GWRE01 USA Wave Race: Blue Storm disc. The Windows player is build/waverace.exe; use the repository root as working directory. Before Play, use the configured original image or keep only the intended .iso in rom/; alternatively set the image-path argument in Change launch details. Use the ordinary invocation unless you deliberately prepare optional VR. Preserve saves/memcard_a.raw as actual player data outside Portcove backup; shader cache is separate. Upstream prohibits redistribution of the game-derived output. Keep the prepared source/data/runtime together; this project offers no complete game package for Portcove to replace.
